title: The Dooars end to end in a week, by car
start: NJP railway station or Bagdogra airport
end: NJP railway station or Bagdogra airport

cost_split.item: Reserved car with driver, 8 days, half share
Forest lodges and good hotels, 7 nights with meals
Private safari jeeps and elephant safari if running, half share

meta_description: 7 nights across the Dooars by private car: Jhalong, Samsing, Gorumara from Lataguri, Jaldapara and Chilapata, in forest lodges, from ₹42,000 per person.
summary: The whole Dooars in a week with your own car: the Jaldhaka river at Jhalong, a cool tea-garden night at Samsing, two nights at Lataguri for Gorumara, two at Madarihat for Jaldapara's rhinos and a last night in Chilapata forest. Private safari jeeps, forest lodges and good hotels. About ₹42,000 per person for two. Parks close mid-June to mid-September.
intro: The Bengal Dooars run along the foot of Bhutan from the Teesta east to the Sankosh river, and most visitors see only Lataguri. This trip goes west to east: up into the river valleys and tea hills first, where nights are cool, then down into the parks, finishing at Chilapata near Hasimara, from where the drive back to NJP is about four hours.

A car and driver for eight days is the big cost, and it buys freedom: no waiting for jeeps, private safari slots and stops wherever the tea or the river looks good. Rooms are the best forest corporation and WBTDC grades, or good private hotels where those are full. Floods in October 2025 hit Gorumara and shut Jaldapara for a time; check current status before you travel.
highlights: Dawn on the Jaldhaka at Jhalong, with Bindu nearby
A tea-garden night at Samsing and Rocky Island
Gorumara's watchtowers, including Medla by bullock cart
Jaldapara's rhinos from a private jeep
A forest night at Mendabari in Chilapata

days.title: NJP to Jhalong
days.text: Your driver meets you at NJP or Bagdogra. Cross the Teesta at Sevoke, drive through Malbazar and Chalsa and climb the Jaldhaka valley to Jhalong. Check into the best grade at the forest corporation's Jholung River Camp. In the afternoon, drive up to Bindu, the last village before Bhutan, where a barrage holds the river; carry ID and do not walk onto the barrage. Evening by the water.

days.title: Jhalong to Samsing via Paren
days.text: Dawn on the river, then climb to Paren for tea and the view over the hills. Drive back down to Chalsa and up through the tea gardens to Samsing, at about 900 m, on the edge of Neora Valley National Park. Check in at the forest corporation's Samsing centre or a good resort nearby. In the afternoon, visit Rocky Island on the Murti and the hanging footbridge at Suntalekhola.

days.title: Down to Lataguri, first tower
days.text: A morning walk in the tea gardens, then down to Lataguri, at about 100 m, warmer and greener. Check into the forest corporation's Lataguri Eco-Tourism Centre or a good resort set back from the highway. In the afternoon, take a private jeep to a Gorumara watchtower, Jatraprasad or the Rhino Observation Point, where rhinos and gaur visit the salt lick near sunset.

days.title: Medla by bullock cart and Chapramari
days.text: Take the dawn slot for Medla, where the last stretch to the tower over the Murti grassland is by bullock cart. Back for breakfast and a long rest. Visit the elephants at Dhupjhora if the timing suits. In the late afternoon, take the Chapramari slot to the waterhole tower, known for the largest gaur herds in West Bengal. Dinner with a local fish thali if you like.

days.title: East through the tea to Madarihat
days.text: Drive east through Chalsa, Nagrakata, Banarhat and Birpara, among some of the largest tea gardens in the Dooars. Stop to watch plucking in season, March to November. Check into the WBTDC Jaldapara Tourist Lodge or a good hotel in Madarihat. Confirm the morning safari and ask whether elephant safaris are running. Afternoon free.

days.title: Jaldapara at dawn, Totopara after
days.text: A private jeep at first light into the Torsa grasslands, where Jaldapara's roughly 330 rhinos graze in the open; take the elephant safari instead if it is running and you have seats. Back for breakfast and rest. In the afternoon, drive about 22 km to Totopara, home of the Toto community, one of India's smallest tribal groups. Visit quietly and ask before photographs.

days.title: Chilapata and Nalraja Garh
days.text: A short drive east to the forest corporation's Mendabari Jungle Lodge in Chilapata. In the afternoon, take a private jeep through dense forest to Nalraja Garh, the brick ruins of an early frontier fort, and along the elephant corridor towards Buxa. Elephants are often close to the track. The evening is quiet, with forest sounds and little else.

days.title: Chilapata to NJP
days.text: A dawn walk in the lodge clearing, breakfast, then the long drive west along the highway through Birpara and Malbazar to Siliguri. Stop for lunch on the way. Reach NJP or Bagdogra by mid-afternoon. Keep a buffer of two to three hours before an evening flight or train; highway traffic near Siliguri can be slow.

includes: Reserved car with driver for 8 days from NJP or Bagdogra and back
Seven nights in forest corporation lodges, the WBTDC lodge and good private hotels, with meals
Private safari jeeps in Gorumara (two), Chapramari, Jaldapara and Chilapata, with fees
Elephant safari at Jaldapara when running
excludes: Room upgrades beyond the best government grade
save_money: Travel as four in one car and fill the safari jeeps; per-person costs fall by about a third.
Swap the Lataguri centre for a good family homestay and save about ₹2,000 per person.
Drop the Chapramari slot if you have already seen gaur in Gorumara.
good_to_know: Parks close from about 16 June to 15 September; check current status before you travel.
Floods in October 2025 damaged parts of Gorumara and shut Jaldapara for a time; check current status before you travel.
Hollong lodge inside Jaldapara burned in June 2024; do not book it unless reopening is confirmed.
Carry ID near the Bhutan border at Bindu and Totopara.

faqs.q: Is a week too long for the Dooars?
faqs.a: Not if you want variety. A week lets you see the river valleys and tea hills as well as the two rhino parks and Chilapata. Most people only do Lataguri in two nights and miss the rest. Each stop here has a different landscape and pace.

faqs.q: How much does an 8-day car cost?
faqs.a: Roughly ₹24,000–28,000 for a car with driver from NJP and back in 2025–26, depending on the vehicle and season, including local runs to safari gates. Split between two, that is about ₹12,000–14,000 each; between four, half that.

faqs.q: Which month is best for this circuit?
faqs.a: November to March for wildlife, cool weather and dry roads. December and January dawns are cold and misty. October is good once parks reopen. April and May are hot in the plains but pleasant at Jhalong and Samsing. Parks close from mid-June to mid-September.

faqs.q: Can we do the circuit in reverse?
faqs.a: Yes. Start at Chilapata, which is about 4–4.5 hours from NJP, and end at Jhalong, about 3 hours away. Safari availability may decide the direction; book the parks first and fit the river valleys around them.

They are clean and simple rather than luxurious, with good settings close to rivers and forests. Book the best grade for attached bathrooms and better beds. Meals are basic but fresh. Where corporation rooms are full, good private resorts nearby fill the gap.

faqs.q: How many safaris does this include?
faqs.a: Five private jeep safaris: two in Gorumara, one in Chapramari, one in Jaldapara and one in Chilapata, plus an elephant safari at Jaldapara if the forest department is running it. Extra slots can be added if available, at about ₹2,500–4,000 per jeep.

Very likely, though never guaranteed. Jaldapara's grasslands give the best odds, with about 330 rhinos. Gorumara's watchtowers add more chances. Dawn and dusk are best. Winter, when grass is cut or burned, gives clearer views.

Layers for cold dawns and warm afternoons, a light jacket, muted safari colours, closed shoes, binoculars, insect repellent, sunscreen, a torch, power bank and ID. Carry some cash, as card machines in the Dooars are unreliable.

Highway towns like Lataguri, Malbazar and Madarihat have good Jio and Airtel coverage. Jhalong, Samsing and Chilapata are patchy, and the parks themselves are weak. Download tickets and maps before you leave Siliguri.
